summary: Dr Brad’s blood pressure and dementia post: target systolic BP below 120 to cut dementia risk 15% and heart attack/stroke risk 27%. Covers DASH diet, salt reduction, exercise, weight loss, and BP medications for hypertension.

summary: Reference on avocado oil: heart health, cholesterol, skin moisturizing, carotenoid absorption. Extra virgin to refined forms; 1-2 tbsp/day. Latex allergy risk; warfarin interaction. Commercial adulteration common. Always discuss with your doctor.

summary: Reference on holy basil (tulsi): stress, anxiety, blood sugar (type 2 diabetes), immune support, cognition. Adults with stress symptoms or type 2 diabetes. Extract 300-1200 mg/day or leaf powder 1000-2500 mg/day. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: L-Citrulline: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on L-citrulline: blood pressure, erectile dysfunction, exercise performance. Best evidence in adults with elevated BP and men with mild ED. Pure form preferred over citrulline malate. Doses 1.5-6 g/day. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Maca: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on maca root: libido, sexual function, erectile dysfunction, sperm quality, menopausal symptoms. Used by men and postmenopausal women. Powder or capsules; 1,500-3,000 mg/day. Thyroid caution; avoid in hormone-sensitive conditions. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Saw Palmetto and Prostate Supplements: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on saw palmetto and prostate supplements: BPH urinary symptoms, hair loss. Lipid extract 320mg/day; beta-sitosterol 30-91mg/day. Evidence mixed; excess zinc linked to prostate cancer risk. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: St. John's Wort: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on St. John's wort: mild to moderate depression, low mood, menopause hot flashes. Comparable to SSRIs; not for severe depression. Extract 300 mg 3x/day. Interacts with contraceptives, statins, warfarin. Always discuss with your doctor.

summary: Dr Brad’s harmful supplements post: calcium raises heart attack risk via artery calcification; iron, vitamin E, vitamin A, and resveratrol lack proven benefit and may harm. Covers blood vessel health, osteoporosis, antioxidants, longevity.

summary: Dr Brad’s morning sunlight post: 30-60 min of bright morning light improves sleep quality, duration, and circadian rhythm via melatonin regulation. Covers light therapy devices, circadian rhythm, insomnia, shift workers, seasonal depression, metabolic syndrome risk.

title: Ginger: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on ginger: nausea (pregnancy, chemotherapy), indigestion, joint pain, blood sugar, menstrual pain. Powder 1-3g/day or extract 100-500mg/day. Caution: bleeding risk with blood thinners, CYP3A4 interactions. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Probiotics: Benefits, Best Strains, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on probiotics: gut health, IBS symptom relief, immune modulation, antibiotic-associated diarrhea prevention; key strains (Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium); dosing and CFU guidance; and safety. Covers bloating, irregular bowel, gut flora restoration. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Psyllium: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on psyllium husk: constipation, LDL cholesterol, blood sugar, IBS, weight management. AGA first-line fiber for chronic constipation; FDA heart health claim. Whole husk or powder, 5-15 g/day. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Taurine: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on taurine. Brad takes it for metabolic benefits: a 2025 meta-analysis of 34 trials found lower blood sugar, blood pressure and blood fats. Levels do not fall with age. 1-3 g/day appears safe. Talk to your doctor first if you take blood-pressure medicines.

title: Amla (Indian Gooseberry): Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on amla (Indian gooseberry): blood sugar, cholesterol, heart health, blood pressure. Adults with type 2 diabetes or high cholesterol. Powder 1-3g/day or extract 500-1000mg/day; caution with diabetes drugs. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: B Vitamins: Benefits, Best Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on B vitamins. Brad: diet first, reach the recommended intake, skip megadoses; Australia warns on B6 over 10 mg a day. B vitamins may slow brain shrinkage with high omega-3. Avoid high-dose niacin and folic acid (outside pregnancy). Talk to your doctor first if pregnant or on medicines.

title: Beetroot: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on beetroot (beet juice): blood pressure, exercise endurance. For hypertension or heart disease. Juice or concentrate, 300-600 mg nitrate/day, 2-3 hrs before exercise. Nitrate content varies by product. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Black Seed Oil: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on black seed oil (Nigella sativa): blood sugar, cholesterol, blood pressure, weight loss, asthma, joint pain. Oil or seed powder; oil 1,000-3,000 mg/day. Interacts with diabetes/BP meds; avoid in pregnancy. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Bone Broth: Benefits, Nutrition, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on bone broth: joint pain, skin wrinkles, muscle mass, sleep (glycine). Most evidence is for collagen peptides, not broth directly. Liquid/powder/capsule; 2-3 cups/day for joints. High sodium content; caution in kidney disease. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Calcium: Benefits, Best Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on calcium: bone health, fracture prevention, osteoporosis. Postmenopausal women, older adults, vegans, and pregnant women most at risk of deficiency. Forms include carbonate and citrate (citrate preferred for PPI users). Typical supplemental doses 500-1,200 mg/day; high doses may raise cardiovascular and kidney stone risk. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Cocoa Flavanols: Benefits, Best Sources, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on cocoa flavanols: heart health, blood pressure, cholesterol, blood sugar. Adults seeking cardiovascular support. Standardized extract (200-500 mg/day) preferred; Dutching destroys up to 90% of flavanols. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Coconut Water: Benefits, Nutrition, Hydration, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on coconut water: natural electrolyte drink for hydration, blood pressure support, exercise recovery. High potassium (400-500 mg/cup); low calorie. Caution: hyperkalemia risk in kidney disease, diabetes, or on ACE inhibitors/potassium-sparing diuretics. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: CoQ10 (Ubiquinol): Benefits, Best Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on CoQ10 (ubiquinol/ubiquinone): heart failure, migraine prevention, statin-related muscle pain and fatigue. Evidence strongest for heart failure (adjunct to medication) and migraine. Ubiquinol preferred over 60; typical dosing 100-300 mg/day with food. Caution with blood thinners, diabetes meds, and during cancer treatment. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Creatine: Benefits, Best Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on creatine. Brad's view: worth considering for body and brain. With resistance training it raises strength and lean mass in older adults; meta-analyses found memory gains, notably in women. Take 5 g/day of monohydrate, no loading. Not advised with severe kidney problems.

title: DHEA: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on DHEA: hormone studied for adrenal insufficiency, depression, vaginal dryness and painful sex (FDA-approved), and bone density in women. Anti-aging evidence weak. Oral 25-50 mg/day with hormone monitoring. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Echinacea: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on echinacea: cold prevention, upper respiratory infections, immune support. E. purpurea aerial extract most studied; ~900 mg/day. Avoid with autoimmune disease or immunosuppressants. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Electrolytes: Benefits, Types, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on electrolytes (sodium, potassium, magnesium, calcium and more). Water is enough for an hour of exercise; replace electrolytes, mainly sodium, after 90+ minutes of strenuous exercise or for diarrhea. Talk to your doctor first with kidney disease, high blood pressure or ACE inhibitors.

title: Extra Virgin Olive Oil: Benefits, Quality, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on extra virgin olive oil: heart health, blood sugar, brain health, inflammation. Most studied at 2-4 tablespoons/day replacing saturated fat. Polyphenol-rich EVOO preferred over refined oil. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: GABA: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on GABA: stress, relaxation, sleep, blood pressure, muscle mass. Limited evidence oral GABA crosses the blood-brain barrier; effects are modest. Dosing ranges 100-3,000 mg depending on use. Avoid in pregnancy and with alcohol. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Garlic: Benefits, Best Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on garlic: high blood pressure, cholesterol, immune support, joint pain, atherosclerosis. Forms include aged garlic extract, powder, black garlic. Bleeding risk; stop before surgery; interacts with warfarin. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Glucosamine, Chondroitin, and Joint Supplements: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on joint supplements: glucosamine, chondroitin, MSM, boswellia, collagen, and curcumin for osteoarthritis and joint pain. For adults with knee or hand pain. Forms, dosing, evidence quality, and safety. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Glycine: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on glycine. Brad's view: in three small trials, 3 g before bed improved rated sleep quality, sleep onset and next-day tiredness; no trial showed fewer wake-ups. GlyNAC corrected glutathione deficiency in older adults. Talk to your doctor first if pregnant or on clozapine.

title: Green Coffee Bean Extract: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on green coffee bean extract: weight loss, blood sugar, blood pressure, cholesterol. Useful for overweight or diabetic adults. Standardized extracts (Svetol/GCA) 200-400 mg/day; key study retracted, evidence modest. Contains caffeine; avoid in pregnancy. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Lutein and Zeaxanthin: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on lutein and zeaxanthin: eye health, macular degeneration (AMD) prevention and slowing, blue light protection, and cataract risk reduction; food sources (leafy greens, egg yolk); dosing (10mg lutein/2mg zeaxanthin); and evidence quality. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Lycopene: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on lycopene: antioxidant, prostate cancer, heart health, blood pressure, skin UV protection, male infertility. Tomato oleoresin or synthetic forms, 6-25 mg/day by indication; always take with fat. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Melatonin: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on melatonin: sleep onset, jet lag, delayed sleep phase, migraine prevention. Children with ASD/ADHD, menopausal women, shift workers. Start low (0.3-3 mg). Caution with diabetes, fractures. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Milk Thistle: Benefits, Best Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on milk thistle (silymarin): liver health, fatty liver, blood sugar in type 2 diabetes, drug-induced liver injury, menopausal hot flashes. Standardized extract 200 mg 2-3x/day. Warfarin interaction risk. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: N-Acetyl Cysteine (NAC): Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on NAC (N-acetyl cysteine): glutathione precursor, liver protection (paracetamol/acetaminophen overdose, NAFLD), respiratory mucus clearance, PCOS, and mental health use; dosing and forms; safety and drug interactions. Covers liver health, lung conditions, PCOS. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Prebiotics: Benefits, Types, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on prebiotics: gut health, constipation, IBS, mood, anxiety, blood sugar, immune support. Most adults get far less than clinical doses. Types: inulin, FOS, GOS, PHGG, psyllium; 2-20 g/day by indication. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Protein Powders: Benefits, Types, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on protein powders. Brad's view: pea protein powder can help when whole foods fall short; his own target is 1.2 g/kg of ideal body weight a day, and with resistance training extra benefit shrinks after 1.3 g/kg. Covers whey, casein, plant types. Kidney disease? Talk to your doctor first.

title: Quercetin: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on quercetin: blood pressure, blood sugar, allergies, joint pain, prostatitis, immune support. Adults with hypertension, insulin resistance, or chronic prostatitis. Forms include free-form, phytosome (better absorbed), EMIQ; 500-1000 mg/day typical. Take with fat. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Red Yeast Rice: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on red yeast rice: LDL cholesterol lowering, heart attack risk reduction. For high cholesterol or statin-intolerant adults. Monacolin K (like lovastatin); 1,200-2,400 mg/day. Muscle, liver, citrinin risks. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Resveratrol: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on resveratrol. Brad says it is not a good strategy: no good evidence it extends life, no effect on mouse lifespan in the Interventions Testing Program, and it reduced exercise benefits in a trial. Avoid in pregnancy; talk to your doctor first if you take blood thinners.

title: Selenium: Benefits, Best Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on selenium: thyroid hormone metabolism, antioxidant defense, immune function, and fertility; food sources (Brazil nuts richest); organic vs inorganic forms; safe dosing range and toxicity ceiling. Covers thyroid disease and low-intake populations. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Shilajit: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on shilajit: testosterone support in older men, bone density in postmenopausal women, exercise fatigue reduction. Most evidence is small, short-term, and industry-funded. Resin (300-2000mg/day) or standardized extract (200-500mg/day). Heavy metal contamination risk — third-party testing essential. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Turmeric and Curcumin: Benefits, Best Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on turmeric and curcumin. Brad steers most patients away from the supplements; curcumin may help ulcerative colitis, knee arthritis, indigestion and prediabetes. Trials used 500-2,000 mg/day. Liver injury reported. Talk to your doctor first, especially if pregnant or on blood thinners.

title: Valerian: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on valerian root: sleep aid, anxiety, relaxation. Mixed evidence for insomnia (modest subjective benefit, weak objective data); not recommended for restless legs. Standardized extract 300-900 mg before bed. Avoid in pregnancy. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Vitamin E: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on vitamin E: antioxidant, fatty liver (NASH), Alzheimer's, heart health. RDA 15 mg/day; diet usually sufficient. Supplements may raise prostate cancer risk; natural vs synthetic forms differ in potency. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: New Study Reveals the BEST Exercise to Reverse Skin Wrinkles
summary: Dr Brad’s skin aging and exercise post: combine resistance and aerobic training for best results. Resistance training boosts dermal thickness via biglycan; aerobic raises IL-15 and reduces inflammation. Both improve elasticity and collagen.

title: Doctor Recommended Intermittent Fasting Hack That ACTUALLY Works
summary: Dr Brad’s intermittent fasting post: IF benefits come from eating less, not timing magic (Cochrane 2021). Circadian meal timing matters — earlier eating improves blood sugar, weight, triglycerides, sleep. Hack: brush teeth 30 min after dinner.

title: Chromium: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on chromium: blood sugar, insulin resistance, PCOS. Most evidence in type 2 diabetes (200-1,000 mcg/day); little benefit in healthy adults. Forms: picolinate (most studied), glycinate. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Collagen: Benefits, Best Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on collagen peptides. A 2026 meta-analysis found they may improve skin hydration and elasticity, but not wrinkles; trials used 0.5 to 10 g a day. Covers forms, joint, bone, muscle and wound evidence, safety, and Brad's current view. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Cranberry: Benefits, Best Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on cranberry: UTI prevention, bladder health. Women with recurrent UTIs, children, men with urinary symptoms. Juice or capsules (36 mg PACs/day); kidney stone risk at high doses; warfarin interaction. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Flaxseed Oil and Omega-6 Oils: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on flaxseed oil, evening primrose, borage, and hemp oils: heart health, blood pressure, acne, dry eye, joint pain. ALA for vegans; whole flaxseed best for blood pressure. GLA may lower seizure threshold. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: L-Tryptophan and 5-HTP: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on L-tryptophan and 5-HTP: sleep, mood, depression, anxiety, migraine, fibromyalgia. Serotonin precursors. L-tryptophan 250mg-1g; 5-HTP 50-300mg at bedtime. Do not combine with SSRIs or MAOIs. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Lion's Mane and Chaga: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on lion's mane and chaga mushrooms: cognitive support, mood, immune function. Lion's mane may help mild cognitive impairment; chaga has no human trials. Forms differ (fruiting body vs mycelium). Chaga carries kidney injury risk from oxalates. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Mangosteen: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on mangosteen: antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, acne, bad breath. Mostly preclinical evidence; two small RCTs only. Pericarp extract 200-400 mg/day. Avoid chronic high-dose juice (lactic acidosis risk). Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Manuka Honey: Benefits, Grading, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on manuka honey: wound healing, acid reflux (GERD), antibacterial, dry eye, oral health. UMF 15+ for therapeutic use; 1-2 tsp/day general wellness, 5g three times daily for GERD. Avoid in infants. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: NAD Boosters (NMN, NR, NADH): Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Dr Brad's view on NAD boosters (NMN, NR, NADH): NMN and NR raise blood NAD+ but trials show no benefit you would notice, and gut bacteria turn both into cheap vitamin B3. He recommends exercise instead. Talk to your doctor first, especially if you have cancer or kidney disease or are pregnant.

title: Olive Leaf Extract: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on olive leaf extract: blood pressure, cholesterol, blood sugar. Evidence mainly in hypertension or type 2 diabetes. Dose by oleuropein content (100-136 mg/day); may interact with BP and diabetes drugs. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Omega-3 Fish Oil: Benefits, Best Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on omega-3 fish oil. Brad takes about 1 g a day for heart and brain health (VITAL: 28% fewer heart attacks) and avoids higher doses linked to atrial fibrillation. Covers forms, major trials, triglycerides and safety. Talk to your doctor first, especially if you take blood thinners.

title: Weight Loss Supplements: Benefits, Evidence, and Safety
summary: Reference on weight loss supplements: appetite, fat burning, metabolism; ephedra/ECA stack harms and ban. For adults with overweight or obesity. Covers caffeine, green tea, CLA, chromium, garcinia cambogia, fiber; most show modest 1-2 kg benefit. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Is the Berberine Hype Justified & Should You Take It?
summary: “Dr Brad’s berberine post: modest evidence for blood sugar and cholesterol in pre-diabetics/type 2 diabetes; not recommended for healthy adults due to possible muscle and testosterone harms. Covers metformin comparison, weight loss, LDL, HbA1c, GLP-1.”

title: How to Correctly Use Hyaluronic Acid to Reverse Wrinkles by 18%
summary: Dr Brad’s hyaluronic acid post: oral HA supplements reduce wrinkles by up to 18.8% in RCTs despite only 0.2% bioavailability — gut bacteria metabolites drive the effect, not direct absorption. Covers sodium hyaluronate 200mg, molecular weight myth, skin aging, wrinkles, safety.

title: Arginine (L-Arginine): Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on L-arginine: blood pressure, erectile dysfunction, heart failure, exercise endurance. Forms: L-arginine HCl (deduct 17% for free arginine), Nitrosigine. Doses 4-15 g/day; contraindicated post-heart attack. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Cholesterol-Lowering Supplements: Benefits, Evidence, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on cholesterol-lowering supplements. Sterols/stanols, red yeast rice and high-dose niacin have the best evidence; psyllium also lowers LDL. Guidelines no longer recommend niacin and recommend no supplement for LDL. Talk to your doctor first, especially if taking a statin or blood thinner.

title: Garcinia Cambogia: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects

title: Which Medications Can Potentially Improve Your Longevity?
summary: Dr Brad's longevity medications post: Brad personally takes finasteride 1mg (prostate cancer prevention) and rosuvastatin 5mg (LDL lowering). Covers statins, ezetimibe, empagliflozin, cholesterol, atherosclerosis, prostate cancer, kidney disease.

title: New Study Links Omega-3 to Increased Heart Arrhythmia Risk
summary: Dr Brad's omega-3 post: supplements at ~1g/day are still worth taking despite a 2024 UK Biobank study showing 133% higher atrial fibrillation risk. Covers EPA, DHA, ALA, fish oil, heart disease, AF risk, megadosing concerns, and the major trials — VITAL (28% MI reduction at 1g/day), STRENGTH (null at 4g/day with AF signal), REDUCE-IT (Vascepa / icosapent ethyl, 25% CVD reduction with the mineral-oil placebo controversy).

title: Which Mistakes Do Most People Make with Magnesium?
summary: Dr Brad's magnesium post: 52% of people are deficient despite normal blood tests, because serum reflects less than 1% of body stores. Covers best forms (glycinate, taurate), elemental dosing (320-420mg RDA), supplement label pitfalls, and links to diet quality.

title: Coconut Oil and MCT Oil: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on coconut oil and MCT oil: weight loss, cognitive support in MCI, skin moisturizing. MCT oil (C8/C10) differs from coconut oil; 5-30 g/day dosing. AHA cautions on LDL and cardiovascular risk. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Can Older Adults and Seniors Still Take Creatine Supplements?
summary: Dr Brad's creatine post: recommends creatine monohydrate for older adults for muscle and potential cognitive/memory benefits. Covers 5g daily dose, kidney safety, hair loss myth, gout, and brain creatine research.

title: Example Home-Based Workout Schedules That Are Scientifically Proven
summary: Dr Brad's home workout post: customize your plan and use key technique principles — concentric-eccentric motion, full range of motion, 8-12 reps over training to failure, and 2+ min rest between sets. Covers resistance training, HIIT, older adults, injury prevention.

title: CLA (Conjugated Linoleic Acid): Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on CLA (conjugated linoleic acid): modest fat loss, body composition, inflammation. Used by overweight adults seeking weight loss or exercise support. Forms: c9,t11 and t10,c12 isomers; typical dose 3-6 g/day. Safety concerns: insulin resistance, reduced HDL, liver effects. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Vitamin D3 and K2: The Benefits, Differences, and Usage
summary: Dr Brad's vitamin D3 and K2 post: evidence is mixed beyond deficiency; Brad takes D3 1000-2000IU and K2 MK-7 90mcg. Covers bone health, cardiovascular disease, osteoporosis, coronary artery calcification, cancer, and drug interactions.

title: Cinnamon: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on cinnamon: blood sugar, cholesterol, inflammation. Adults with type 2 diabetes or prediabetes. Cassia vs Ceylon forms; Ceylon safer (lower coumarin). Dosing 1-6g/day bark or 250-500mg extract. Coumarin liver/bleeding risk; interacts with blood thinners. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Magnesium L-Threonate and Its Effects on Sleep Quality
summary: Dr Brad's magnesium L-threonate post: evidence for sleep benefits is weak — small studies exist but are low quality or not specific to this form. Covers magnesium forms, drug interactions (statins, gabapentin), dosing safety, insomnia.

title: Choline: Benefits, Best Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on choline: memory, fatty liver, brain health in pregnancy. Deficiency common in women and older adults. CDP-choline preferred for cognition; choline bitartrate raises TMAO and cardiovascular risk; alpha-GPC linked to stroke. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Chia Seed: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on chia seeds: high fiber, plant-based omega-3 (ALA), blood sugar, blood pressure, gut and bone health. Dose 1-2 tbsp/day; soak before eating to avoid choking. Caution if kidney stone history (oxalates). Always discuss with your doctor.

title: CBD (Cannabidiol): Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on CBD (cannabidiol): anxiety, insomnia, pain, and epilepsy/seizures. Adults use it for social anxiety (300 mg), sleep problems (160 mg), and chronic pain. Forms: full-spectrum, isolate, oils, topicals. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Bilberry: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on bilberry: retinopathy, dry eye, blood sugar, vascular health. Best evidence for diabetic/hypertensive retinopathy. Look for 36% anthocyanoside extract. Caution with blood thinners and diabetes meds. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Baobab: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on baobab: high fiber, gut health, blood sugar after meals, vitamin C, iron absorption. Adults wanting a fiber or nutrient boost. Powder 5-30 g/day; start low to avoid bloating. Caution in kidney disease. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Astaxanthin: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on astaxanthin: antioxidant carotenoid studied for skin UV protection, triglycerides, HDL, joint pain, exercise recovery, and eye fatigue. Natural algal form (4-18 mg/day) used in trials; take with fat. Evidence is mixed and preliminary. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Apple Cider Vinegar: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on apple cider vinegar: blood sugar control, weight loss, cholesterol. Studied in insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, overweight adults. Liquid form only (pills ineffective); 1-2 tbsp/day diluted in water. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Alpha Lipoic Acid: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on alpha-lipoic acid (ALA): nerve pain, blood sugar control, weight loss. Best evidence for diabetic neuropathy and insulin sensitivity. Forms: racemic or R-ALA, 300-1800 mg/day. Heartburn common. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Alginates: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on alginates (Gaviscon, sodium alginate): heartburn, acid reflux, GERD, throat reflux. Safe in pregnancy. Liquid, chewable, or capsule; 200–1000 mg after meals up to 4x daily. Separate from meds 2h. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: African Mango: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on African mango (Irvingia gabonensis): weight loss, cholesterol, blood sugar. Marketed for obesity and weight management; very weak evidence — only 3 small trials from one research group. IGOB131 extract 300mg/day studied. GI side effects possible. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Acetyl-L-Carnitine: Benefits, Forms, Dosing, and Side Effects
summary: Reference on acetyl-L-carnitine (ALCAR): memory, nerve pain, depression, blood pressure. May help older adults with early cognitive decline, diabetic neuropathy, low mood. Typical dose 1-3 g/day. Avoid if on chemotherapy or with thyroid/seizure disorders. Always discuss with your doctor.

title: Diet: Clinical Dietary Guidance
summary: Diet — what is the best diet, what should I eat, Mediterranean, DASH, Portfolio diet, best proteins, saturated fat, sodium, fibre, ultra-processed food, added sugar, alcohol. Covers 9 heart-healthy dietary features, priority foods (legumes for protein + fibre + potassium), specific daily serving targets, and IBS/IBD dietary management including low-FODMAP guidance. Compiled from AHA 2026 dietary guidance, US DGA 2020–2025 food group targets, and Brad's clinical framework. Brad's divergences on omega-3 supplementation and alcohol noted.

title: Exercise: Clinical Exercise Guidance
summary: Exercise — how much per week, what intensity, cardio vs resistance training, strength and power training, specific guidance for blood pressure, knee arthritis, diabetes, cognition, and bone density. Covers minimum effective dose, the high-volume plaque paradox, and Brad's baseline of at least 150 min/wk moderate cardio (or 75 vigorous, or a mix) + 2–3 resistance sessions. Built from AHA 2024 resistance exercise statement, US Physical Activity Guidelines, WHO 2020, Schoenfeld meta-analyses, 2025 UK Biobank dose-response data, and condition-specific RCTs.

title: Sleep: Clinical Insomnia Guidance
summary: Sleep and insomnia — can't sleep, trouble staying asleep, sleep hygiene, CBT-I as first-line, melatonin dosing, magnesium glycinate, glycine. Covers ICSD-3-TR diagnosis, CBT-I techniques, pharmacotherapy drug classes (DORAs, Z-drugs, doxepin, trazodone) with dosing tables, and supplement evidence.
